title: Kernel dispatch presets and compile-time tuning for MoE/GQA/MHA to smooth tail latency
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a lightweight, reproducible mechanism to pick and publish a small set of compilation presets and dispatch heuristics per model variant (MoE, GQA, MHA) that reduce tail latency variance across customer workloads while keeping token cost and mean latency within current SLOs. This ticket covers the engineering design, a PoC implementation in the compiler router, telemetry to validate regressions, and a staged rollout for pinned model versions.

Problem statement:
- MoE models show large per-request latency variance due to expert imbalance and dynamic shard load.
- GQA-like architectures with grouped attention have divergent kernel hotspots depending on batch shapes.
- MHA models with long context suffer from kernel path explosion when codegen chooses suboptimal matmul/attention kernels for certain seq_len distributions.
- Current onboarding publishes many candidate kernels; operators then see spikes in p50/p99 that are hard to correlate.

Goal:
- Produce a per-model "dispatch preset" artifact that contains: a) preferred kernel family, b) compile flags (vector width, tiling hints), c) KV-cache memory layout preference, and d) a fallback policy with latency/cost thresholds.
- Make presets small (<= 4 entries) and include a runtime scoring heuristic that favors lower tail-latency for high-priority customers.
- Publish presets to the profile service and wire them into the staged rollout pipeline so Dedicated/Private customers can pin them per model-version.

Acceptance criteria:
- A dispatch-presets proto format defined and stored in profile-service (backwards compatible with current profile schema).
- Compiler router can accept a preset and produce deterministic kernel selection for a representative set of inputs.
- Automated e2e benchmark harness that compares default vs preset selection across curated workloads and emits p50/p95/p99 and cost delta.
- Telemetry dashboards that surface per-preset p50/p95/p99, failure rates, and expert imbalance metrics for MoE.
- Rollout plan and kill-switch in place; per-version pinning supported in console UI/workflow.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Option A (aggressive per-arch presets): create many presets specific to micro-architectures (e.g., AMP-1, AMP-2). Pro: best perf. Con: explosion of artifacts and higher maintenance cost.
- Option B (workload class presets): categorize presets by typical seq_len/batch shapes (short, medium, long, streaming). Pro: smaller surface area. Con: may miss tail cases.
- Our pragmatic approach: hybrid presets (Option B by default, with opt-in micro-arch refinement for priority customers).
- We prefer an immutable preset artifact referenced by model-version (not by model name alone) to allow safe rollbacks.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Spec: define dispatch-preset JSON schema (or proto) and add validation in profile-service.  -> small schema so it can be embedded in release notes.
2) Compiler router: add a PresetResolver that maps request attributes (model-version, seq_len_est, batch_size_est, customer_tier) to a candidate list.
3) Kernel selector: implement deterministic tie-breakers based on preset weights and latency-cost bias.
4) Telemetry: extend runtime traces to emit chosen preset id, reason-code, and per-kernel timings.
5) Bench harness: add curated scenarios for MoE expert imbalance, GQA grouped attention shapes, and long-context MHA. Generate nightly comparisons.
6) Console integration: surface preset name/version on model page and add pin/unpin controls for Dedicated/Private.

PoC details / perf knobs tried so far:
- Implemented a small Preset JSON (3 fields): family, flags, fallback_threshold_ms (proof-of-concept branch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4812).
- Ran local e2e harness for a 12B MoE with synthetic skewed routing; preset that forces expert affinity + KV layout change reduced p99 by ~28% but increased mean token latency by ~6% and marginal cost +2.4%.
- For GQA we tested a preset that prefers blocked-MMA kernels for medium seq_len ranges; this improved p95 by ~14% across batch sizes 1-8.
- MHA long-context preset that forces an attention-rewrite reduced memory allocations and avoided a pathological kernel that inflated p99 for seq_len > 4096.

Telemetry & validation plan:
- Add new metrics: preset_id, preset_reason_code, chosen_kernel_id, kernel_latency_ms, expert_load_stddev, kv_hit_ratio.
- Create dashboard (Grafana) with: per-preset p50/p95/p99, customer-tier splits, and rollback alert if p99 regresses > 15% over baseline for 1 hour.
- Add automatic smoke checks in CI that run the harness for a small set of seeds and fail the PR if any preset causes > 20% p99 regression.

Rollout plan:
- Canary (internal): 10% of internal traffic pinned to the new preset for 48h.
- Beta customers: opt-in via console flag for a week; collect telemetry and run qualitative checks with SEs.
- Gradual rollout: 5% increments with automated safeguards and immediate global rollback if high-severity alerts trigger.

Open questions / risks:
- How to represent multi-kernel bundles in a single preset while keeping runtime decision cheap? (We may need a small decision tree encoded as prioritized kernel ids.)
- Preset proliferation risk: need a TTL/garbage collection policy in profile-service.
- Interactions with autoscaling: presets that favor high-throughput kernels may increase GPU saturation and affect neighboring workloads.

Next steps (short-term):
- Finalize preset schema and land profile-service validation (owner: @sophia-zhang).
- Merge minimal PresetResolver into compiler router and wire flag to opt-in per-model-version. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4812).
- Expand benchmark scenarios and add nightly job (owner: @miguel-ortega).
